sanskrit: sahaḥ kṛtir vipāpmā ca puṇyakṛt pāvanas tathā grāmniḥ kṣemaḥ samūhaś ca divyasānus tathaiva ca
english: Sahas, Kṛti, Vipāpman, Puṇyakṛt, and Pāvana likewise; Grāmaṇi, Kṣema, Samūha, and Divyasānu as well.

sanskrit: vivasvān vīryavān hrīmān kīrtimān kṛta eva ca vipūrvaḥ somapūrvaś ca sūryaśrīś ceti nāmataḥ
english: Vivasvat, Vīryavat, Hrīmat, Kīrtimat, and Kṛta; Vipūrva, Somapūrva, and Sūryaśrī — so they are named.

sanskrit: somapaḥ sūryasāvitro dattātmā puṣkarīyakaḥ uṣṇīnābho nabhodaś ca viśvāyur dīptir eva ca
english: Somapa, Sūryasāvitra, Dattātman, Puṣkarīyaka; Uṣṇīnābha, Nabhoda, Viśvāyu, and Dīpti too.

sanskrit: camūharaḥ suveṣaś ca vyomāriḥ śaṃkaro bhavaḥ īśaḥ kartā kṛtir dakṣo bhuvano divyakarmakṛt
english: Camūhara and Suveṣa, Vyomāri, Śaṃkara, Bhava; Īśa, Kartṛ, Kṛti, Dakṣa, Bhuvana, and Divyakarmakṛt.

sanskrit: gaṇitaḥ pañcavīryaś ca ādityo raśmimāṃs tathā saptakṛt somavarcāś ca viśvakṛt kavir eva ca
english: Gaṇita and Pañcavīrya, Āditya, and Raśmimat; Saptakṛt, Somavarcas, Viśvakṛt, and Kavi too.

sanskrit: anugoptā sugoptā ca naptā ceśvara eva ca jitātmā munivīryaś ca dīptalomā bhayaṃkaraḥ
english: Anugoptṛ and Sugoptṛ, Naptṛ, and Īśvara; Jitātman, Munivīrya, Dīptaloman, and Bhayaṃkara.

sanskrit: atikarmā pratītaś ca pradātā cāṃśumāṃs tathā śailābhaḥ paramakrodhī dhīroṣṇī bhūpatis tathā
english: Atikarman and Pratīta, Pradātṛ, and Aṃśumat; Śailābha, Paramakrodhin, Dhīroṣṇi, and Bhūpati.

sanskrit: srajī vajrī varī caiva viśvedevāḥ sanātanāḥ kīrtitās te mahābhāgāḥ kālasya gatigocarāḥ
english: Srajin, Vajrin, and Varin — these are the eternal Viśvedevas, the greatly blessed ones, now celebrated, who move within the range of time's course.

sanskrit: aśrāddheyāni dhānyāni kodravāḥ pulakās tathā hiṅgu dravyeṣu śākeṣu palāṇḍuṃ laśunaṃ tathā
english: Among grains, kodrava and pulaka are unfit for the śrāddha rite; among condiments, asafoetida; among vegetables, the onion and the garlic.

sanskrit: palāṇḍuḥ saubhañjanakas tathā gṛñjanakādayaḥ kūṣmāṇḍajātyalābuṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ lavaṇam eva ca
english: The onion, the drumstick plant, the carrot and their kind, the gourd-fruit and the bottle-gourd, and black salt as well.

sanskrit: grāmyaṃ vārāhamāṃsaṃ ca yac caivāprokṣitaṃ bhavet kṛṣṇājājī viḍaś caiva śītapākī tathaiva ca aṅkurādyās tathā varjyā iha śṛṅgāṭakāni ca
english: The flesh of the domestic boar, and whatever has not been consecrated, black cumin, biḍa salt, and the slow-ripening melon, sprouted shoots and the like, and water-chestnuts — these too are to be shunned here.

sanskrit: varjayel lavaṇaṃ sarvaṃ tathā jambūphalāni ca avakṣutāvaruditaṃ tathā śrāddheṣu varjayet
english: One should avoid all manufactured salt, and likewise the fruit of the rose-apple; and at śrāddha rites one should reject whatever has been sneezed or wept upon.

sanskrit: nivāpe havyakavye vā garhitaṃ ca śvadarśanam pitaraś caiva devāś ca nābhinandanti tad dhaviḥ
english: At an offering of food, of oblations to the gods or to the fathers, the sight of a dog is to be deplored; neither the fathers nor the gods take pleasure in such an oblation.

sanskrit: caṇḍālaśvapacau varjyau nivāpe samupasthite kāṣāyavāsī kuṣṭhī vā patito brahmahāpi vā
english: When the offering of food is set forth, the Caṇḍāla and the dog-eater must be kept away, as must the wearer of ochre robes, the leper, the outcaste, and even the slayer of a brahmin.

sanskrit: saṃkīrṇayonir vipraś ca saṃbandhī patitaś ca yaḥ varjanīyā budhair ete nivāpe samupasthite
english: A brahmin of mixed birth, and a kinsman who has fallen from his estate — these the wise must exclude when the offering of food is set forth.

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā bhagavān svavaṃśajam ṛṣiṃ purā pitāmahasabhāṃ divyāṃ jagāmātris tapodhanaḥ
english: Having thus spoken of old to the sage born of his own line, the venerable Atri, rich in austerity, departed to the divine assembly hall of the Grandfather.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tathā vidhau pravṛtte tu sarva eva maharṣayaḥ pitṛyajñān akurvanta vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Bhīṣma said: When the rite had been set in motion in this manner, all the great sages performed the sacrifices to the fathers with action prescribed by ordinance.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo dharmanityās tu kṛtvā nivapanāny uta tarpaṇaṃ cāpy akurvanta tīrthāmbhobhir yatavratāḥ
english: The sages, ever devoted to dharma, having made their food-offerings, performed too the libation of water from sacred fords, steadfast in their vows.

sanskrit: nivāpair dīyamānaiś ca cāturvarṇyena bhārata tarpitāḥ pitaro devās te nānnaṃ jarayanti vai
english: Gratified by the offerings of food given by the four orders, O Bhārata, the fathers and the gods could not, however, digest the food.

sanskrit: ajīrṇenābhihanyante te devāḥ pitṛbhiḥ saha somam evābhyapadyanta nivāpānnābhipīḍitāḥ
english: Stricken by indigestion, those gods together with the fathers, oppressed by the offered food, betook themselves to Soma.

sanskrit: te 'bruvan somam āsādya pitaro 'jīrṇapīḍitāḥ nivāpānnena pīḍyāmaḥ śreyo no 'tra vidhīyatām
english: Reaching Soma, the fathers, afflicted with indigestion, said: "We are tormented by the offered food; let some remedy be devised for us in this matter."

sanskrit: tān somaḥ pratyuvācātha śreyaś ced īpsitaṃ surāḥ svayaṃbhūsadanaṃ yāta sa vaḥ śreyo vidhāsyati
english: Then Soma answered them: "If you desire a remedy, O gods, go to the abode of the Self-Existent; he will ordain what is best for you."

sanskrit: te somavacanād devāḥ pitṛbhiḥ saha bhārata meruśṛṅge samāsīnaṃ pitāmaham upāgaman
english: At Soma's word, those gods together with the fathers, O Bhārata, approached the Grandfather, who was seated upon the peak of Meru.

sanskrit: pitara ūcuḥ nivāpānnena bhagavan bhṛśaṃ pīḍyāmahe vayam prasādaṃ kuru no deva śreyo naḥ saṃvidhīyatām
english: The fathers said: "By the offered food, O Lord, we are sorely tormented. Show us your grace, O God; let some remedy be ordained for us."

sanskrit: iti teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā svayaṃbhūr idam abravīt eṣa me pārśvato vahnir yuṣmacchreyo vidhāsyati
english: Hearing these words of theirs, the Self-Existent spoke thus: "Here at my side is Fire; he will ordain what is best for you."

sanskrit: agnir uvāca sahitās tāta bhokṣyāmo nivāpe samupasthite jarayiṣyatha cāpy annaṃ mayā sārdhaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: Agni said: "Together, dear ones, we shall eat when the offering of food is set forth, and along with me you shall digest the food — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu pitaras tatas te vijvarābhavan etasmāt kāraṇāc cāgneḥ prāktanaṃ dīyate nṛpa
english: Hearing this, the fathers were thereupon freed of their distress; and for this very reason, O king, the foremost portion is given to Agni.

sanskrit: nivapte cāgnipūrve vai nivāpe puruṣarṣabha na brahmarākṣasās taṃ vai nivāpaṃ dharṣayanty uta rakṣāṃsi cāpavartante sthite deve vibhāvasau
english: When the offering is made with Agni first, O bull among men, the brahma-rākṣasas do not defile that offering, and the demons turn away when the god of radiant light is present.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ piṇḍaṃ pitur dadyāt tato dadyāt pitāmahe prapitāmahāya ca tata eṣa śrāddhavidhiḥ smṛtaḥ
english: First one should offer the rice-ball to the father, then to the grandfather, and then to the great-grandfather: this is held to be the ordinance of the śrāddha.

sanskrit: brūyāc chrāddhe ca sāvitrīṃ piṇḍe piṇḍe samāhitaḥ somāyeti ca vaktavyaṃ tathā pitṛmateti ca
english: At the śrāddha, with collected mind, one should recite the Sāvitrī over each rice-ball; one should say "to Soma," and likewise "to him attended by the fathers."

sanskrit: rajasvalā ca yā nārī vyaṅgitā karṇayoś ca yā nivāpe nopatiṣṭheta saṃgrāhyā nānyavaṃśajāḥ
english: A woman in her courses, or one maimed in her ears, should not attend at the offering; nor are those of another lineage to be admitted.

sanskrit: jalaṃ prataramāṇaś ca kīrtayeta pitāmahān nadīm āsādya kurvīta pitṝṇāṃ piṇḍatarpaṇam
english: While crossing a body of water, one should call to mind the grandfathers; and upon reaching a river, one should perform the rice-ball offering and libation to the fathers.

sanskrit: pūrvaṃ svavaṃśajānāṃ tu kṛtvādbhis tarpaṇaṃ punaḥ suhṛtsaṃbandhivargāṇāṃ tato dadyāj jalāñjalim
english: First having made the water-libation to those born of one's own line, one should then offer a handful of water to the company of friends and kinsmen.

sanskrit: kalmāṣagoyugenātha yuktena tarato jalam pitaro 'bhilaṣante vai nāvaṃ cāpy adhirohataḥ sadā nāvi jalaṃ tajjñāḥ prayacchanti samāhitāḥ
english: When one crosses the water yoked to a pair of dappled oxen, the fathers indeed long for him, and as he climbs aboard the boat; ever upon the boat those who know offer the water-libation with collected minds.

sanskrit: māsārdhe kṛṣṇapakṣasya kuryān nivapanāni vai puṣṭir āyus tathā vīryaṃ śrīś caiva pitṛvartinaḥ
english: In the half-month of the dark fortnight one should make the food-offerings; for nourishment, long life, vigor, and prosperity attend upon him who is devoted to the fathers.

sanskrit: pitāmahaḥ pulastyaś ca vasiṣṭhaḥ pulahas tathā aṅgirāś ca kratuś caiva kaśyapaś ca mahān ṛṣiḥ ete kurukulaśreṣṭha mahāyogeśvarāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: The Grandfather, Pulastya, Vasiṣṭha, and Pulaha, Aṅgiras, Kratu, and the great sage Kaśyapa — these, O best of the Kuru line, are remembered as the mighty lords of yoga.

sanskrit: ete ca pitaro rājann eṣa śrāddhavidhiḥ paraḥ pretās tu piṇḍasaṃbandhān mucyante tena karmaṇā
english: These too are the fathers, O king; this is the supreme ordinance of the śrāddha. The departed, bound to the rice-ball offerings, are by that act set free.

sanskrit: ity eṣā puruṣaśreṣṭha śrāddhotpattir yathāgamam khyāpitā pūrvanirdiṣṭā dānaṃ vakṣyāmy ataḥ param
english: Thus, O best of men, has the origin of the śrāddha, as it was first set forth, been declared to you according to tradition. Of the gift of charity I shall now speak hereafter.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca dvijātayo vratopetā havis te yadi bhuñjate annaṃ brāhmaṇakāmāya katham etat pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: If the twice-born, bound by their vows, eat the oblation — food given out of desire to please the brahmins — how can this be, O grandfather?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca avedoktavratāś caiva bhuñjānāḥ kāryakāriṇaḥ vedokteṣu tu bhuñjānā vrataluptā yudhiṣṭhira
english: Bhīṣma said: Those bound by vows not enjoined in the Veda, if they eat, are merely doers of their duty; but those who eat while under vows enjoined in the Veda, O Yudhiṣṭhira, have broken their vow.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yad idaṃ tapa ity āhur upavāsaṃ pṛthagjanāḥ tapaḥ syād etad iha vai tapo 'nyad vāpi kiṃ bhavet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: That fasting which the common folk here call austerity — is this indeed austerity, or might true austerity be something else?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca māsārdhamāsau nopavased yat tapo manyate janaḥ ātmatantropaghātī yo na tapasvī na dharmavit
english: Bhīṣma said: The fasting for a month or half a month that people deem austerity — he who thereby injures his own constitution is neither an ascetic nor a knower of dharma.

sanskrit: tyāgasyāpi ca saṃpattiḥ śiṣyate tapa uttamam sadopavāsī ca bhaved brahmacārī tathaiva ca
english: The very perfection of renunciation is taught to be the highest austerity; one may be ever a faster and likewise ever a celibate.

sanskrit: muniś ca syāt sadā vipro devāṃś caiva sadā yajet kuṭumbiko dharmakāmaḥ sadāsvapnaś ca bhārata
english: A brahmin may be ever a sage, and ever may he sacrifice to the gods, though he be a householder devoted to dharma, and ever wakeful, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: amṛtāśī sadā ca syāt pavitrī ca sadā bhavet ṛtavādī sadā ca syān niyataś ca sadā bhavet
english: He may be ever an eater of ambrosia, and ever may he be pure; ever a speaker of truth he may be, and ever may he be self-restrained.

sanskrit: vighasāśī sadā ca syāt sadā caivātithipriyaḥ amāṃsāśī sadā ca syāt pavitrī ca sadā bhavet
english: He may be ever an eater of the remnants, and ever loving toward his guests; ever an abstainer from flesh he may be, and ever may he be pure.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ sadopavāsī syād brahmacārī ca pārthiva vighasāśī kathaṃ ca syāt kathaṃ caivātithipriyaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How may one be ever a faster and a celibate, O king? And how may one be an eater of the remnants, and how a lover of guests?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca antarā sāyamāśaṃ ca prātarāśaṃ tathaiva ca sadopavāsī bhavati yo na bhuṅkte 'ntarā punaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: He who does not eat again in between the evening meal and the morning meal becomes ever a faster.

sanskrit: bhāryāṃ gacchan brahmacārī sadā bhavati caiva ha ṛtavādī sadā ca syād dānaśīlaś ca mānavaḥ
english: Approaching his wife only in her season, a man becomes ever a celibate; and a man given to charity becomes ever a speaker of truth.

sanskrit: abhakṣayan vṛthā māṃsam amāṃsāśī bhavaty uta dānaṃ dadat pavitrī syād asvapnaś ca divāsvapan
english: By not eating flesh in vain, one becomes an abstainer from flesh; by giving in charity, one becomes pure; and even sleeping by day, one remains free of sleep.

sanskrit: bhṛtyātithiṣu yo bhuṅkte bhuktavatsu naraḥ sadā amṛtaṃ kevalaṃ bhuṅkte iti viddhi yudhiṣṭhira
english: The man who ever eats only after his dependents and guests have eaten — know, O Yudhiṣṭhira, that he eats nothing but ambrosia.

sanskrit: abhuktavatsu nāśnāti brāhmaṇeṣu tu yo naraḥ abhojanena tenāsya jitaḥ svargo bhavaty uta
english: The man who does not eat while the brahmins have not yet eaten — by that very abstinence heaven is won by him.

sanskrit: devebhyaś ca pitṛbhyaś ca bhṛtyebhyo 'tithibhiḥ saha avaśiṣṭāni yo bhuṅkte tam āhur vighasāśinam
english: He who eats what is left over after the gods, the fathers, his dependents, and his guests — him they call an eater of the remnants.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ lokā hy aparyantāḥ sadane brahmaṇaḥ smṛtāḥ upasthitā hy apsarobhir gandharvaiś ca janādhipa
english: For such men, boundless worlds in the abode of Brahmā are remembered, attended by Apsarases and Gandharvas, O lord of men.

sanskrit: devatātithibhiḥ sārdhaṃ pitṛbhiś copabhuñjate ramante putrapautraiś ca teṣāṃ gatir anuttamā
english: Together with the deities, the guests, and the fathers they feast, and they take delight with their sons and grandsons; theirs is a course beyond all surpassing.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca brāhmaṇebhyaḥ prayacchanti dānāni vividhāni ca dātṛpratigrahītror vā ko viśeṣaḥ pitāmaha
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Men bestow various gifts upon the brahmins; between the giver and the receiver, which is the more excellent, O grandfather?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sādhor yaḥ pratigṛhṇīyāt tathaivāsādhuto dvijaḥ guṇavaty alpadoṣaḥ syān nirguṇe tu nimajjati
english: Bhīṣma said: The twice-born who accepts a gift from a virtuous man, or likewise from one who is not virtuous, incurs little fault if the giver is endowed with merit, but he sinks down if the giver is devoid of it.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam vṛṣādarbheś ca saṃvādaṃ saptarṣīṇāṃ ca bhārata
english: On this point, too, they recount this ancient tale, the dialogue between Vṛṣādarbhi and the Seven Sages, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: kaśyapo 'trir vasiṣṭhaś ca bharadvājo 'tha gautamaḥ viśvāmitro jamadagniḥ sādhvī caivāpy arundhatī
english: Kaśyapa, Atri, and Vasiṣṭha, then Bharadvāja and Gautama, Viśvāmitra, Jamadagni, and the virtuous Arundhatī as well.

sanskrit: sarveṣām atha teṣāṃ tu gaṇḍābhūt karmakārikā śūdraḥ paśusakhaś caiva bhartā cāsyā babhūva ha
english: Now Gaṇḍā was the serving-maid of all of them, and the Śūdra Paśusakha was her husband.

sanskrit: te vai sarve tapasyantaḥ purā cerur mahīm imām samādhinopaśikṣanto brahmalokaṃ sanātanam
english: All of them, performing austerities, of old wandered over this earth, striving through meditation toward the eternal world of Brahmā.

sanskrit: athābhavad anāvṛṣṭir mahatī kurunandana kṛcchraprāṇo 'bhavad yatra loko 'yaṃ vai kṣudhānvitaḥ
english: Then there came a great drought, O delight of the Kurus, in which this world was reduced to a hard struggle for life and gripped by hunger.

sanskrit: kasmiṃś cic ca purā yajñe yājyena śibisūnunā dakṣiṇārthe 'tha ṛtvigbhyo dattaḥ putro nijaḥ kila
english: And once, of old, at a certain sacrifice, the son of Śibi, the patron of the rite, gave his own son to the officiating priests as a sacrificial fee.

sanskrit: tasmin kāle 'tha so 'lpāyur diṣṭāntam agamat prabho te taṃ kṣudhābhisaṃtaptāḥ parivāryopatasthire
english: At that time, O lord, that short-lived boy came to the end ordained by fate; and they, scorched by hunger, surrounded him and stood near.

sanskrit: yājyātmajam atho dṛṣṭvā gatāsum ṛṣisattamāḥ apacanta tadā sthālyāṃ kṣudhārtāḥ kila bhārata
english: Then, seeing the patron's son bereft of life, those most excellent sages, tormented by hunger, set to cooking him in a pot, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nirādye martyaloke 'sminn ātmānaṃ te parīpsavaḥ kṛcchrām āpedire vṛttim annahetos tapasvinaḥ
english: In this world of mortals where there was nothing to eat, those ascetics, seeking to preserve their own lives, fell into a wretched mode of living for the sake of food.

sanskrit: aṭamāno 'tha tān mārge pacamānān mahīpatiḥ rājā śaibyo vṛṣādarbhiḥ kliśyamānān dadarśa ha
english: Now the lord of the earth, the Śaibya king Vṛṣādarbhi, roaming along the road, beheld them cooking, sorely afflicted.

sanskrit: vṛṣādarbhir uvāca pratigrahas tārayati puṣṭir vai pratigṛhṇatām mayi yad vidyate vittaṃ tac chṛṇudhvaṃ tapodhanāḥ
english: Vṛṣādarbhi said: Accepting a gift brings deliverance; it is indeed a nourishment for those who receive. Hear, O you rich in austerity, what wealth is to be found with me.

sanskrit: priyo hi me brāhmaṇo yācamāno; dadyām ahaṃ vo 'śvatarīsahasram ekaikaśaḥ savṛṣāḥ saṃprasūtāḥ; sarveṣāṃ vai śīghragāḥ śvetalomāḥ
english: Dear to me indeed is the brahmin who asks; I would give you a thousand she-mules, each one with its sire and brought to birth, all of them swift-going and white of coat.

sanskrit: kulaṃbharān anaḍuhaḥ śataṃśatān; dhuryāñ śubhān sarvaśo 'haṃ dadāni pṛthvīvāhān pīvarāṃś caiva tāvad; agryā gṛṣṭyo dhenavaḥ suvratāś ca
english: Bulls that sustain a family, by the hundred upon hundred, draught-oxen fair and fit for the yoke I would give you wholly, broad and well-fed bearers of the earth, and as many milch-cows, choice young heifers, gentle of disposition.

sanskrit: varān grāmān vrīhiyavaṃ rasāṃś ca; ratnaṃ cānyad durlabhaṃ kiṃ dadāni mā smābhakṣye bhāvam evaṃ kurudhvaṃ; puṣṭyarthaṃ vai kiṃ prayacchāmy ahaṃ vaḥ
english: Choice villages, rice and barley and savory things, and other jewels hard to obtain — what shall I give? Do not turn your minds to forbidden food; for your nourishment, what shall I bestow upon you?

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ rājan pratigraho rājño madhvāsvādo viṣopamaḥ taj jānamānaḥ kasmāt tvaṃ kuruṣe naḥ pralobhanam
english: The sages said: O king, a gift from a king is sweet to the taste as honey, yet like poison. Knowing this, why do you set temptation before us?

sanskrit: kṣatraṃ hi daivatam iva brāhmaṇaṃ samupāśritam amalo hy eṣa tapasā prītaḥ prīṇāti devatāḥ
english: The warrior-order leans upon the brahmin as upon a deity; for this brahmin, made spotless by austerity and well pleased, gives pleasure to the gods themselves.

sanskrit: ahnāpīha tapo jātu brāhmaṇasyopajāyate tad dāva iva nirdahyāt prāpto rājapratigrahaḥ
english: Sometimes the austerity of a brahmin is born here in but a single day; and a king's gift, once received, would burn that away as a forest fire consumes.

sanskrit: kuśalaṃ saha dānena rājann astu sadā tava arthibhyo dīyatāṃ sarvam ity uktvā te tato yayuḥ
english: "May welfare, along with your giving, be ever yours, O king; let all be given to those who seek it" — having so spoken, they then departed.

sanskrit: apakvam eva tan māṃsam abhūt teṣāṃ ca dhīmatām atha hitvā yayuḥ sarve vanam āhārakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: That flesh of theirs, wise as they were, remained even yet uncooked; and so, abandoning it, they all went off into the forest, still longing for food.

sanskrit: tataḥ pracoditā rājñā vanaṃ gatvāsya mantriṇaḥ pracīyodumbarāṇi sma dānaṃ dātuṃ pracakramuḥ
english: Then, urged on by the king, his ministers went into the forest and, gathering wild figs, set about giving them as a gift.

sanskrit: udumbarāṇy athānyāni hemagarbhāṇy upāharan bhṛtyās teṣāṃ tatas tāni pragrāhitum upādravan
english: Now they brought up other wild figs, gold-laden within, and the king's servants then ran forward to press these upon the sages to accept.

sanskrit: gurūṇīti viditvātha na grāhyāṇy atrir abravīt na sma he mūḍhavijñānā na sma he mandabuddhayaḥ haimānīmāni jānīmaḥ pratibuddhāḥ sma jāgṛmaḥ
english: Knowing them to be heavy, Atri declared they were not to be taken: "We are no men of deluded understanding, ho! We are no dullards of feeble wit! We know these are made of gold; we are awake, we keep watch."

sanskrit: iha hy etad upādattaṃ pretya syāt kaṭukodayam apratigrāhyam evaitat pretya ceha sukhepsunā
english: For this, taken up here, would yield a bitter fruit hereafter; by one who longs for happiness in the world beyond and in this one, it is simply not to be accepted.
